commitResults.messageTitle: Add a single tag without replacing existing tags
commitResults.messageBody:
Members need a way to gain a tag while retaining their existing roles.
The edit command rejects tag arguments and cannot perform this update.

Add tagadd with one displayed index and one tag per command. Reuse
case-insensitive tag identity, allow repeated additions, and show all
members afterward to match edit. Cover parsing, preservation, and
filtered-list targeting with tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove a single tag while preserving other tags
commitResults.messageBody:
Members need to lose individual roles without replacing their tag set.

Add tagremove with one displayed index and one case-insensitive tag.
Allow removal of the last tag and treat an absent tag as a successful
unchanged record. Show all members after completion, matching edit.

Cover parsing, case matching, preservation, empty tags, and filtered
indices with command and parser tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document and verify single-member tag updates
commitResults.messageBody:
The new tag commands need usage guidance and persistence coverage.

Document syntax, case matching, unchanged-record success, and the return
to the full member list. Add manual acceptance cases and integration
tests that reload saved records after repeated tag updates.

All new tests, both Checkstyle tasks, and repository checks pass.
The full suite passes 320 of 321 tests; the existing image-loading test
fails because the JavaFX native libraries are Intel-only on this ARM Mac.

commitResults.messageTitle: Preserve member status when updating tags
commitResults.messageBody:
The member constructor used by tag commands defaults status to active.
After integration with member status, any tag update reactivates an
archived member, even when the requested tag change leaves tags intact.

Carry the existing status into both replacement records. Add regression
tests for archived members covering addition, removal, duplicate
addition, and absent-tag removal.

All four regressions fail before the fix and pass afterward. Tag tests,
integration tests, Checkstyle, and repository checks pass. The full
suite passes 329 of 330 tests; the existing JavaFX image-loading test
fails due to incompatible native libraries on the ARM development Mac.

commitResults.messageTitle: Rename tag commands to tag and untag
commitResults.messageBody:
The tagadd and tagremove command names require extra typing for
routine member tagging.

Rename them to tag and untag while preserving their arguments and
behaviour. Update edit guidance, command examples and existing parser
and integration tests to use the shorter names.

Validation: Gradle check and coverage pass, with one skipped test.
Repository formatting checks pass.
Fix Archived status display
Enable assertions in build.gradle

commitResults.messageTitle: Preserve data after JSON loading errors
commitResults.messageBody:
A failed data load starts an empty address book, and the next successful
command can overwrite the original file. One invalid record therefore
puts every saved member at risk.

Recover valid records and report rejected records with their original
positions. Show a startup warning and block changes and saving after
partial or failed loading, while keeping viewing and searching
available. Require repair and a successful restart before restoring
normal saving.

Add regression tests for recovery, duplicate records, malformed files,
read failures, and file preservation through commands and shutdown.

Validation: Gradle check passes with 419 tests passed and one skipped.
Repository formatting checks also pass.

The guides describe an empty directory that can overwrite an invalid
file after a successful command. That no longer reflects recovery.

Describe partial record loading, startup warnings, save protection, and
the repair-and-restart workflow. Update the storage design and manual
testing instructions to cover the protected session behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add initial member use cases to Developer Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide still has an AddressBook delete-person use case
and does not describe member addition or lookup. This leaves the
secretary's basic interactions with NUSocietyDesk unclear.

Describe member deletion, addition, and name-based lookup as textual
use cases. Keep their extensions aligned with AB3 behavior so the
requirements can evolve alongside the product.
Normalize tag identity

Find accepts only unprefixed name keywords. Explicit field selection
provides consistent syntax for phone and email searches to build on.

Accept an optional n/ prefix while preserving existing name matching.
Reject empty values, repeated prefixes, and text before a prefix.
Allow person predicates so later fields can reuse the same command.

Refs #54

Find searches names only, so secretaries cannot locate members using
a remembered phone number.

Support p/ substring searches, including short digit sequences.
Reject empty values, repeated prefixes, and combined name and phone
searches. Preserve existing name searches and reuse the results view.

Phone searches treat multiple fragments as one substring and return no
matches. This can make unsupported input look like a valid search.

Reject phone values containing whitespace-separated fragments and show
an explanatory error. Add parser coverage for spaces, tabs, and line
breaks to keep the single-substring rule consistent.

The guides describe name searches only, leaving the new n/ and p/
syntax and phone search restrictions unexplained.

Document search formats, matching rules, invalid inputs, and examples
in the User Guide. Extend UC03 with both search fields, result counts,
and error flows so both guides match the implemented behavior.
Restrict member email addresses to the @u.nus.edu domain

commitResults.messageTitle: Add email substring search to find
commitResults.messageBody:
Secretaries who remember part of a member's email need a way to
locate the member without knowing their name or phone number.

Extend find with e/ for case-insensitive substring matching.
Preserve single-field searches and reject empty values, repeated
prefixes, and multiple fragments.

Update the guides and tests to document and verify the behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Shorten the find command usage message
commitResults.messageBody:
The find usage message is lengthy and difficult to scan in the
results panel.

Replace the detailed explanation with command formats and examples
so users can correct their input quickly.

The UI uses inherited AB3 wording that differs from the project name.

Update the window title and command messages to reflect NUSocietyDesk
and its member directory.
Update version number to v1.3

commitResults.messageTitle: Update help link and User Guide screenshot
commitResults.messageBody:
The help window links to the upstream AB3 User Guide.

Point it to the NUSocietyDesk User Guide so users receive the correct
instructions, and refresh the help screenshot to match.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject non-digit input in phone searches
commitResults.messageBody:
Phone searches accept invalid characters and report zero matches,
leaving users without an explanation.

Validate search substrings as ASCII digits after existing format
checks. Preserve short fragments, leading zeros, and error precedence.

Add parser and integration tests for invalid input and unchanged
results. Document the restriction in the User Guide.
Support partial CSV import with rejection feedback
Preserve member data when saving fails

commitResults.messageTitle: Log find command completion and match count
commitResults.messageBody:
Command execution logs do not show search outcomes.

Add an INFO completion message with the match count through the
existing logging framework to make search outcomes easier to trace.

Secretaries need to locate members by their assigned tags.

Support find t/TAG using existing case-insensitive tag identity.
Reject multiple tags and mixed fields to keep searches unambiguous.
Cover matching, validation, and state preservation with tests.

Uppercase prefixes fall through to name search and can silently
produce no matches.

Reject uppercase search prefixes with guidance to use lowercase
forms. Preserve case-insensitive matching of search values.

Unknown search prefixes fall through to name searches and can
silently produce no matches.

Validate prefixes against the four supported fields and report
unsupported prefixes explicitly. Preserve lowercase guidance for
uppercase variants and literal values attached to valid prefixes.

Add regression tests and update both guides.
Update version number to v1.4
Add session-only command history

commitResults.messageTitle: Restrict prefixed name searches to one keyword
commitResults.messageBody:
Prefixed search arguments need to represent one condition for
future combined searches.

Reject multiple n/ keywords and suggest unprefixed OR searches.
Preserve existing name matching and prefix validation. Route
multiline find input through search validation for clear errors.

Update usage messages and add regression tests for whitespace,
matching, and preservation of results, records, and saved data.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update search documentation and manual tests
commitResults.messageBody:
The guides need to reflect single-keyword prefixed name searches
and provide phone-search verification steps.

Clarify name-search syntax, examples, and error handling. Update
UC03 and add manual tests for name and phone searches, including
matching rules and preservation of results and saved data.

Bob's number contains both 9 and 91, so both searches match
Alice and Bob.

Use p/89 to demonstrate a two-digit search matching only Bob.
Clarify that p/ selects the phone field and matches substrings
anywhere in the number.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test multiline find routing for all search fields
commitResults.messageBody:
Direct field-parser tests bypass multiline command routing.

Add routing tests for phone, email, and tag searches with
whitespace-separated values. Assert field-specific errors for
spaces, tabs, LF, and CRLF.

The find command accepts only one field, limiting how secretaries can
narrow member searches.

Add findall with AND matching across repeated name, phone, email and
tag conditions. Reuse field validation and the existing search command
to keep ordinary find behavior consistent.

Test matching, validation, routing and preservation of results and
saved data when a search is rejected.

Secretaries need to find members matching alternative criteria across
contact fields and tags.

Add findany with OR matching across explicitly prefixed conditions.
Share condition parsing with findall and validate every condition
before filtering, even when another condition would match.

Test overlapping matches, incomplete members, command routing and
preservation of previous results and saved data after invalid input.

The guides describe only single-field searches and need to explain
how secretaries can combine conditions.

Add concise syntax, examples and command summaries for AND/OR searches.
Update implementation notes, the search use case and manual checks
to reflect the supported behavior.

Command validation prevents unsupported prefixes from reaching the
shared condition parser, leaving its defensive guard uncovered.

Add a direct test that verifies the exception type and message.

The guide explains search behavior without illustrating how the
search commands share their execution path.

Add a partial class diagram covering parsers, FindCommand, and
predicate composition. Follow course UML conventions and use one
field predicate as an example so the diagram remains useful as
search fields evolve.
Document Command History with a class diagram

Multiline PlantUML tags disrupt Markdown parsing in MarkBind.

Keep the status-view and search diagram tags on single lines
so the remaining sections render correctly.

commitResults.messageTitle: Normalize tags and remove tag editing from edit
commitResults.messageBody:
Tags treat case variants as distinct values, and edit replaces the
entire tag set. This causes inconsistent labels and accidental loss
of unrelated tags.

Normalize tag names to lowercase across creation and loading.
Preserve existing tags during edits and reject tag arguments with
guidance to use the planned tagadd and tagremove commands.

and no Checkstyle violations.

Secretaries with existing member directories must add contacts one at a
time. A validated CSV import makes adoption practical without losing
membership statuses or partially changing the directory on bad input.

Add the import command and a fixed UTF-8 CSV reader. Validate all
records and duplicate emails before applying the combined directory,
preserving existing members, imported statuses, and canonical tags.
Keep the source file unchanged and reuse the existing JSON persistence
flow.

Cover quoted fields, file paths, invalid records, duplicate emails,
rejected-import preservation, and persistence with focused tests.
Verify all 382 tests and Checkstyle using Java 25 Gradle check.

commitResults.messageTitle: Protect CSV import sources from automatic saving
commitResults.messageBody:
An import source can point to the directory save file through a direct
path or an alias. Automatic saving would then overwrite the source and
break the promise that importing leaves the input file unchanged.

Reject save-file sources before executing import. Compare normalized
paths and file identity to cover aliases and links. Verify that rejected
imports preserve records, filters, and source and save-file contents.

Verify all 384 tests and Checkstyle using Java 25 Gradle check.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document CSV import and provide a sample template
commitResults.messageBody:
Secretaries need a predictable CSV layout and clear guidance on why an
entire import is rejected instead of silently accepting some records.

Document the import command, fixed headers, required statuses, tag
syntax, duplicate rules, and source preservation. Explain error record
numbers and the existing behavior when automatic saving fails.

Describe the implementation and focused manual GUI checks in the
Developer Guide. Add a sample CSV containing active and archived members
and validate it with the production reader. GUI checks are not run.

Email identity needs a stable representation that does not depend on the
user's locale. Store emails in lowercase using Locale.ROOT while preserving
the existing rule that whitespace is invalid.

Cover canonical equality, locale independence, whitespace rejection, and
distinct aliases with focused unit tests.

Name-based identity prevents different members with the same name from being
stored. Define member identity using canonical email so names and phone
numbers can be shared when emails differ.

Cover same-name updates and normalized email conflicts in the model tests.

Generic duplicate errors do not tell users which member owns an email.
Report the canonical email and existing member name for add and edit
conflicts, including records outside the current filtered list.

Update command tests to verify the actionable message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Report stored email conflicts by record
commitResults.messageBody:
Stored members now use canonical email as their identity, so loading must
accept namesakes while rejecting case-insensitive email conflicts. Include
record positions in the first loading error to make manual correction
practical.

Update the duplicate fixture and storage conversion tests for the new rule.

Representative data should demonstrate that members may share a name and
phone number when their canonical emails differ. Add a pair of namesakes so
the identity rule is visible on first launch.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle invalid address book JSON structures
commitResults.messageBody:
Malformed JSON structures can bypass the existing startup fallback by
failing outside the expected data-loading exception path.

Validate the root and persons shapes before conversion so storage
consistently reports a DataLoadingException.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document email identity and loading behavior
commitResults.messageBody:
Email now identifies members and storage reports duplicate saved
addresses, while the guides still describe phone number duplicates.

Update command rules, storage notes, and manual checks to match the
committed behavior, including the empty address book startup fallback.

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover sample members and null storage records
commitResults.messageBody:
The sample namesake records and null JSON guard are not exercised by

Exercise both sample members and assert that a null record reports its
one-based position.
Fix small bug in Person model

commitResults.messageTitle: Restrict member emails to the NUS student domain
commitResults.messageBody:
Member email validation accepts general domains, but the directory
requires addresses ending with @u.nus.edu.

Enforce the exact domain through the shared Email validator while
preserving lowercase normalization and existing local-part rules.
Update command examples, sample data, test fixtures, and both guides
to match the accepted format.

Cover other-domain rejection and verify that invalid add and edit
commands leave records, filters, and saved data unchanged.
Add all-or-nothing CSV member import

commitResults.messageTitle: Support members with optional contact details
commitResults.messageBody:
Member records require a name, phone and address even when those
details are unavailable. The model needs to represent their absence
before email-only registration can be supported.

Represent optional contact details with Optional values while keeping
email required and preserving email-based identity. Update storage,
search, editing and cards to handle incomplete records.

Persist absent details as JSON nulls, accept omitted properties and
retain validation for supplied values. Preserve compatibility with
complete records and show clear placeholders on member cards.

Update model and storage tests and adapt existing test helpers to the
optional fields.

commitResults.messageTitle: Allow adding members with only a NUS email
commitResults.messageBody:
The add command requires complete contact details even when the
secretary only knows a member's NUS email.

Make name, phone and address independently optional while retaining
validation for supplied values and rejecting repeated contact prefixes.

Show only supplied details and nonempty tags in add and edit
confirmations to avoid clutter from missing-field placeholders.

Cover optional-field combinations and validation in parser tests.
Update command tests, usage messages and both guides to document
email-only registration and completing details through edit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify member details in command confirmations
commitResults.messageBody:
Tag confirmations include missing-field placeholders and empty tag
sections, while name labels differ between commands.

Reuse the supplied-details formatter for tagadd and tagremove to
omit missing contact fields and hide the Tags section when empty.
Retain the added or removed tag in the confirmation.

Standardize supplied names as Name: <person name> across add, edit,
tag and delete confirmations using a shared prefix constant.

Update tag-command tests and both guides to cover the revised
messages for incomplete members and removal of the final tag.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add label prefix constants for member detail feedback
commitResults.messageBody:
Introduce PHONE_PREFIX, EMAIL_PREFIX, ADDRESS_PREFIX and TAGS_PREFIX
and use them when building the list of details shown in the command
feedback message, replacing the inline string literals.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show only provided details in delete confirmations
commitResults.messageBody:
Delete confirmations currently show placeholders for missing member details.
Use the same supplied-details format as add confirmations, and remove
the formatter that is no longer used. Cover email-only members in the
tests and document the updated output.

The command box has no history state to support recalling submissions
while preserving unsent input and edits.

Add a deque-based history helper with a 100-entry limit, oldest-first
eviction and consecutive duplicate suppression. Preserve drafts and
temporary edits while browsing, and support selecting failed commands
without introducing a duplicate draft position.

Keep this state independent of JavaFX so navigation can be tested
without a display. Add metadata-only logging, invariant assertions and
JUnit coverage, including a Gradle check with assertions disabled.

commitResults.messageTitle: Enable command history in the command box
commitResults.messageBody:
Handle Up and Down in the command box to recall and edit submitted
commands. Record commands before execution so failed commands remain
available, and keep the current draft when navigating history.

Add UI tests for navigation, edits, failures, duplicates, and the
100-command limit. Share JavaFX setup across the UI tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document command history behavior and verification
commitResults.messageBody:
Explain command recall, editable entries, draft restoration, failure
handling, and the 100-command limit in the user and developer guides.

Document the history design, logging and assertions, automated test
commands, and manual verification scenarios.
Document CSV import and save recovery with UML
Document the shared search design

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Command History class diagram to DG
commitResults.messageBody:
The Command History documentation relies on prose to explain ownership
and navigation state, making the class relationships harder to follow.

Add a class diagram showing history ownership, the draft snapshot,
and the execution callback. Organize the surrounding explanation and
add examples of draft restoration, temporary edits, and navigation
after a failed command.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject arguments to the help command
commitResults.messageBody:
The help command ignores trailing arguments, so inputs such as
help 1 open the window despite the command taking no parameters.

Delegate argument validation to HelpCommandParser and reject
nonempty arguments with the existing format error. Preserve
surrounding whitespace and test parser dispatch and validation.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show an offline command reference in Help
commitResults.messageBody:
Help only provides a User Guide URL, requiring users to leave the
application to check command syntax.

Add descriptions, usage, and examples for all 16 commands beneath
the existing guide link. Make the reference scrollable and the
window resizable while retaining Copy URL and F1/menu access.

Skip saving member data when help runs so it remains available
during recovery and saving failures. Enable result text wrapping
and test reference content, popup behavior, and data preservation.

The guides describe URL-only help and ignored help arguments.

Describe the offline reference, strict no-argument syntax, and
retained online guide access. Add design and manual testing notes,
refresh the known-issue wording, and include exit in the command
summary.
Fix Developer Guide Markdown rendering

Update the default storage path, test paths, fixtures, and documentation
to use nusocietydesk.json consistently.

Long punctuation-separated email local-parts can overflow the regex
matcher and leave command failures without validation feedback.

Limit normalized local-parts to 64 UTF-16 units before regex matching.
Share validation errors across commands, CSV import and JSON loading.
Cover length boundaries, failure recovery and the reported payload.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document email length validation and recovery
commitResults.messageBody:
The email length limit affects command input, CSV import and saved
records, so users and maintainers need consistent guidance.

Describe the limit, feedback and rejection behavior in the User Guide.
Explain validation ordering and caller handling in the Developer Guide,
and add manual boundary and overflow regression checks.
